label: Exploratory Weekly Configuration v0.1 (per-disease residual search) — Technical / Retrospective Evaluation Only
authorization_reference: Per-disease SARIMA order selected offline by SARIMANNAR/residual_search.py as each disease's lowest-AIC specification among candidates whose residuals leave structure for the residual network; NNAR size re-tuned per disease by stage 2 on that specification. No adviser approval.
implementation_choices: Each disease uses the single lowest-AIC SARIMA specification whose residuals leave structure for the residual network (Ljung-Box rejecting white noise), and an NNAR size re-tuned by stage 2 against that same specification, not against the search's own accuracy-ranked pick. The search builds its NNAR input as a contiguous window of the last L residuals; this application indexes discrete lags instead, so L is expressed as the equivalent lags [1..L]. AIC and forecast accuracy diverge on these series: the residual search ranks them with Spearman correlation -0.4 (Dengue), 0.4 (Measles-Rubella) and 1.0 (Leptospirosis), and on Measles-Rubella the AIC specification forecasts 2.5x worse standalone than the accuracy-ranked one while the hybrid is nearly unchanged. Each specification was re-fitted here under enforce_stationarity=True with blanks preserved, so the resulting fit is verified at request time rather than assumed. The Dengue search dropped 9 null week-53 observations, which shifts positional seasonal alignment. Unsearched diseases fall back to the `default` block. Blanks remain missing and are never imputed; week 53 is preserved in sequence. These are documented technical safeguards, not adviser-approved statistical rules.
